symbols.def: Common degree of the interference network.

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Known simple undirected interference graph on \(V_n\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Fixed number \(r=2\) of DTE target exposures.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Index for all-control and isolated-treatment exposures.

symbols.name: e_{i,k}
symbols.def: \(e_{i,0}=\mathbf0_{\widetilde N_i}\), while \(e_{i,1}\) assigns one to \(i\) and zero to its neighbors.

symbols.def: All laws on the assignment space.

symbols.name: \mathcal Q_n
symbols.def: All joint laws on a retained record and assignment.

symbols.name: R_2(G)
symbols.def: Minimax risk over all assignment laws and assignment-only estimators.

symbols.def: Graph of incompatible DTE target exposures.

symbols.name: \operatorname{MIS}(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G))

symbols.def: Generic estimator in the observation game.

assumptions.condition: The known graph \(G\) is simple, undirected, and \(d\)-regular on \(V_n\).
The potential-outcome schedule \(Y\) is fixed before assignment.
For every \(i\in V_n\) and \(z,z'\in\mathcal Z_n\), equality \(z|_{\widetilde N_i}=z'|_{\widetilde N_i}\) implies \(Y_i(z)=Y_i(z')\).
The class \(\mathsf{NP}\) is not contained in \(\mathsf{BPP}\).

definitions.name: Published second-moment ANI class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_2(G)=\{Y\in\prod_{i\in V_n}\mathbb R^{\mathcal Z_n}:Y\text{ satisfies }\texttt{ass:ani}\text{ and }\texttt{ass:q2-moment}\text{ for this }n,G\}\).

definitions.name: Two-layer DTE conflict graph
definitions.construction: \(V(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G))=V_n\times\{0,1\}\) and \(E(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G))=\{\{(i,0),(i,1)\}:i\in V_n\}\cup\{\{(i,1),(j,1)\}:\{i,j\}\in E_G\}\cup\{\{(i,1),(j,0)\},\{(i,0),(j,1)\}:\{i,j\}\in E_G\}\). There are no control--control edges.

definitions.name: Deterministic certified factor
definitions.construction: \(\kappa_{\mathrm{DTE}}(d)=\inf\{a\ge1:\exists\mathsf A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{poly}}\ \forall n\ \forall G\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ \Pr_{\mathsf A}[\operatorname{Risk}_2(\Psi_{\mathsf A}(G),G)\le U_{\mathsf A}(G)\le aR_2(G)]\ge2/3\}\).

definitions.name: Recorded DTE Conflict Graph Design
definitions.construction: Compute \(\pi\); draw \(W\); retain \(\omega=W\); initialize \(z=\mathbf0\); and in importance order enforce \(z|_{\widetilde N_i}=e_{i,k}\) whenever \(E^*_{i,k}\) occurs. The joint law is \(Q_{\mathrm{CGD}}(G)\).

definitions.name: Exact-regular DTE reduction handle
definitions.construction: Degree-deficit switchings plus layerwise posterior-risk duality: start from \(J\) and \(\xi\), expose every filled edge, track the donor completeness cover and all-large-sets density after each switching, and formulate the resulting \(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G)\) channel as a two-layer Bayes experiment with prior \(\Pi_{\mathrm{NO}}\).

definitions.name: Universal lower-certificate handle
definitions.construction: Start from Bayes posterior risk for the maximal-independent-set channel, compress priors using the two-layer symmetries and separate layer moment constraints, and dualize the posterior-variance problem into a finite witness.

statements.statement: For every \(\Psi=(Q,\gamma_{\mathrm{rec}})\) and \(Y\in\mathcal M_2(G)\), \(\mathbb E_{z\sim P_Q}[(\bar\gamma_Q(z,Y(z))-\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y))^2]\le\mathbb E_{(\omega,z)\sim Q}[(\gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}(\omega,z,Y(z))-\tau_{\mathrm{DTE}}(Y))^2]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{\Psi\in\mathcal Q_n\times\Gamma_n^{\mathrm{rec}}}\operatorname{Risk}_2(\Psi,G)=R_2(G)\).
statements.justification: Conditional Jensen reconciles recorded design coins with the assignment-only benchmark.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026 uses this conditional-expectation pattern inside its conflict-game proof; the explicit equality fixes the procedure information set.
statements.consumer: Conflict Graph Design can be compared with exactly \(R_2(G)\).

statements.statement: For every network \(G\), \(R_2(G)=\mathfrak R_2(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G))\), with simultaneous constraints \(n^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,0}^2\le1\) and \(n^{-1}\sum_i u_{i,1}^2\le1\).
statements.justification: The identity fixes the unrestricted value and rules out an independence-number proxy.
statements.gap: This is already known from KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5.
statements.consumer: Any reduction must prove both value inequalities for this exact game.

statements.statement: The edges of \(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G)\) are exactly the vertical pairs; the treated--treated pair and both cross-layer pairs for every \(\{i,j\}\in E_G\); and no control--control pairs. Thus each edge added to regularize \(G\) creates exactly three nonvertical DTE conflicts.
statements.justification: This identity shows why graph regularization is not value-neutral.
statements.gap: An abstract regular two-layer product need not obey the DTE edge predicate.
statements.consumer: A valid reduction must audit every degree-filling edge in the observation channel.

statements.statement: Already-known calibration: for every \(G\in\mathcal G_{n,d}\), KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024, Algorithm 1, Proposition 3.5, and Theorem 4.1 give \((Q_{\mathrm{CGD}}(G),\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{CGD}})\), unbiasedness, and \(\operatorname{Risk}_2((Q_{\mathrm{CGD}}(G),\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{CGD}}),G)\le U_{\mathrm{CGD}}(G)=25(d+1)/n\). KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Corollary 1.1 and Section 5.1, give \(R_2(G)\gtrsim\sqrt{d+1}/n\), so \(U_{\mathrm{CGD}}(G)\le C_0\sqrt d R_2(G)\).
statements.justification: The cited results give the implementable upper half of the comparison.
statements.gap: This direct combination is already known and is not new theorem content.
statements.consumer: Experimenters obtain a realizable design, estimator, and pre-assignment certificate.

statements.statement: Already-known sanity check: if \(E_G=\varnothing\), then \(H_{\mathrm{DTE}}(G)\) is a matching and \(R_2(G)=\Theta(n^{-1})\). The \(r=2\) construction has \(\Pr(W_i=e_{i,1})=\Pr(W_i=e_{i,0})=1/4\), induces independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\) treatment, and its modified desired-event estimator has risk of order \(n^{-1}\).
statements.justification: The specialization checks the defined two-exposure construction.
statements.gap: This is not novel; Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 sharpen the no-interference problem.
statements.consumer: It verifies that the formalism creates no artificial loss without interference.

statements.statement: Can the degree-deficit switching and posterior-risk handle be completed into an explicit dossier? Given \(J\) and \(\xi\), construct in randomized polynomial time a labeled simple \(G\in\mathcal G_{n,d}\) with \(d=\Delta^{2+o(1)}\), \(n=\operatorname{poly}(m,\Delta)\), explicit parity and multiplicity handling, and success probability at least \(2/3\); prove that donor completeness and all-large-sets soundness survive every regularization edge; map each \(J\in\mathsf{YES}_{\Delta}\) to a law on realizable assignments and a recorded \(\Psi\) with stated inclusion probabilities and \(\operatorname{Risk}_2(\Psi,G)\le C_{\mathrm{gap}}\sqrt d/n\); and give an explicit layer-normalized \(\Pi_{\mathrm{NO}}\) or finite dual witness proving \(R_2(G)\ge c_{\mathrm{gap}}d/[n(\log d)^{K_{\mathrm{gap}}}]\) for every \(J\in\mathsf{NO}_{\Delta}\), against every assignment law and estimator? The dossier must include a nondegenerate finite YES/NO calculation with full network edges, degree table, DTE-conflict adjacencies, realized assignments, and numerical risks.
statements.justification: This is the missing object required before a square-root hardness frontier can be asserted.
statements.gap: AustrinKhotSafra2011 ends at maximum degree, while ChalermsookLaekhanukitNanongkai2013 gives an abstract product from a different regular promise; neither gives this DTE risk separation.
statements.consumer: A solution would support a certificate-aware lower frontier and the one-sided numerical question underlying Conjecture 2 of KandirosHarshawSavje2026.

statements.statement: Can the posterior-risk handle produce, for every two-layer DTE conflict graph, a polynomial-size dual witness whose value lower-bounds \(R_2(G)\) and is within a universal constant factor, while preserving assignment-law realizability on the primal side?
statements.justification: An explicit dual would expose the graph functional hidden by the unrestricted minimax representation.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026 leaves the functional implicit; Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 use no-interference symmetries unavailable here.
statements.consumer: A checkable lower certificate would give Conflict Graph Design and CauseIS an instance-wise optimality gap.

sampling_model.design: A procedure uses a joint law \(Q\) on retained coins \(\omega\) and assignment \(z\); the benchmark ranges over all assignment laws and assignment-only estimators.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, network \(G\), and potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment is randomized once; DTE contrasts isolated treatment and all-control.
sampling_model.overlap: The modified estimator uses desired-event probabilities \(p_{i,k}\), evaluated from retained \(W\).
sampling_model.algorithmic_randomness: The deterministic factor requires \(\Pr[\operatorname{Risk}_2\le U\le aR_2]\ge2/3\) uniformly over every size and regular input.

estimand_functional: \(\kappa_{\mathrm{DTE}}(d)=\inf\{a\ge1:\exists\mathsf A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{poly}}\ \forall n\ \forall G\in\mathcal G_{n,d},\ \Pr_{\mathsf A}[\operatorname{Risk}_2(\Psi_{\mathsf A}(G),G)\le U_{\mathsf A}(G)\le aR_2(G)]\ge2/3\}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Conjecture 2 asks for degree-to-the-one-half-minus-slack hardness for regular-network DTE minimax risk.
Theorem 4.1 gives maximum-degree independent-set hardness after sampling and high-degree edge deletion.
Section 5.2 gives a regular abstract bipartite induced-matching product from an already-regular donor.
Algorithm 1, Proposition 3.5, and Theorem 4.1 give Conflict Graph Design, unbiasedness, and a spectral variance bound.
Theorem 1 reduces bounded no-interference unrestricted minimax design to a finite convex problem.
The main reduction solves unrestricted binary-outcome no-interference minimax risk through a low-dimensional problem.
CauseIS selects an independent set and benchmarks DTE through peer-effect cancellation and simulations.

tldr: The square-root computational lower frontier for regular-network DTE is not asserted because the required value-preserving reduction has no explicit construction or unrestricted-risk witness. The core retains the exact recorded-coin benchmark, published maximal-independent-set representation, deterministic uniform definition of \(\kappa_{\mathrm{DTE}}(d)\), and already-known \(O(\sqrt d)\) Conflict Graph Design calibration. The new mathematical object is stated honestly as an open construction dossier: exact regularization preserving donor completeness and density, DTE-conflict realization, a realizable low-risk YES design, and a layer-normalized all-design, all-estimator NO witness on the same image.

project_justification.gap: The literature supplies a maximum-degree donor gap, an abstract regular induced-matching product, the exact DTE observation game, and the Conflict Graph Design upper bound, but no construction simultaneously preserves exact regularity, DTE realizability, and two-sided unrestricted risk.
project_justification.niche: The viable object is the missing construction-and-witness dossier rather than an asserted hardness frontier.
project_justification.fill: The open question fixes the switching invariants, exposure law, inclusion-probability calculation, layerwise prior or dual inequalities, and finite audit that a future kernel must supply.

related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026, Proposition 2.2 and Appendix A.5, supplies the unrestricted maximal-independent-set representation; Corollary 1.1 and Section 5.1 give the regular-DTE lower benchmark; Conjecture 2 is only a target for one-sided numerical hardness. KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024, Algorithm 1, Proposition 3.5, and Theorem 4.1, supplies the recorded randomization, modified Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness, and spectral variance bound. AustrinKhotSafra2011, Theorem 4.1, leaves a maximum-degree graph after edge deletion, not an exact-regular graph. ChalermsookLaekhanukitNanongkai2013, Section 5.2, starts from a different regular promise and outputs an abstract induced-matching product, not a DTE conflict graph or risk separation. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 eliminate unrestricted estimators only without interference. FatemiZheleva2023 is the applied consumer because CauseIS uses one independent set without a universal-risk certificate; CaiZhangAiroldi2024 imposes stronger outcome structure.
technical_internal_limitation: Exact degree filling changes the statistical instance: every added base edge creates the treated--treated conflict and both cross-layer conflicts. A degree-deficit gadget can therefore remove the YES exposure cover or create sparse large subsets violating NO density. Donor independence number alone does not provide a distribution covering both exposure coordinates with the inclusion probabilities needed for \(C\sqrt d/n\) risk. Conversely, small independent sets or density alone do not lower-bound posterior risk uniformly over every maximal-independent-set law and nonlinear estimator. No switching invariant, completeness distribution, layerwise least-favourable prior, or finite matched risk calculation is available to close these gaps.
honest_scope: The recorded-coin Rao--Blackwell bridge, exact two-layer game representation, exhaustive DTE adjacency relation, Conflict Graph Design upper calibration, and empty-network reduction are settled or already-known components. The exact-regular donor reduction and two-sided risk separation are open. No certificate-aware lower bound, equality \(\kappa_{\mathrm{DTE}}(d)=d^{1/2+o(1)}\), or numerical hardness corollary is claimed. A later numerical result must use the one-sided event \(R_2(G)\le\widetilde R_{\mathsf B}(G)\le d^{1/2-\varepsilon}R_2(G)\) with median and reduction-trial majority amplification; the displayed promise-gap algebra would support only a quarter-degree exponent under a symmetric convention.
message: The frontier is retracted and the angle needs a pivot: the exact-regular DTE reduction, realizable YES exposure law, unrestricted-estimator NO witness, and required finite risk audit cannot be exhibited from the preserved kernel or cited donor constructions.
